- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.52 in Example 1), then correct downward.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Late-period forecasts (last 5–10 days) are consistently too high, suggesting model lacks short-term volatility capture.
- Model underreacts to sudden drops — true outcomes show sharper declines than forecasted (e.g., 72.50 → 65.81 in Example 1).
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in high volatility periods — model overconfident in upward trends.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or event-driven corrections — e.g., 68.96 → 62.41 in Example 4.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements — especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts peak too early and then drop too abruptly.
- Model underestimates downward momentum after mid-forecast period — true prices often dip more than forecasted.
